title: Proton transfer reactions
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: R3.1.4#xt1 term and clue written for the game; R3.1.6#xt2 term and clue written for the game; R3.1.8#xt2 term and clue written for the game; R3.1#c02 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: R3.1#q12, R3.1#q14, R3.1#q13, R3.1#q15, R3.1#q32, R3.1#q33, R3.1#q16, R3.1#q17, R3.1#q18, R3.1#q20, R3.1#q22, R3.1#q24.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: pH
items.clue: Equal to –log₁₀[H⁺]; a decrease of one unit means a tenfold increase in [H⁺].

items.label: Weak acid
items.clue: A proton donor that is only partially ionized in aqueous solution, such as CH₃COOH.

items.label: Equivalence point
items.clue: Stage of a titration at which acid and base have been mixed in exactly stoichiometric amounts.

items.label: Brønsted–Lowry base
items.clue: A species that accepts a proton (H⁺) from another species, using a lone pair of electrons to form a bond to the proton.

questions.stem: Aqueous ethanoic acid is added to solid sodium carbonate until the reaction stops. What are the products of the reaction?

options.text: sodium ethanoate and water, with no gas
sodium ethanoate, hydrogen and carbon dioxide
none, as weak acids do not react with carbonates
sodium ethanoate, water and carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂. The carbonate ion accepts two protons, forming H₂O and CO₂.

questions.stem: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ HCl(aq) is placed in a flask and 25.0 cm³ of distilled water is added. The mixture is then titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH(aq). At what pH does the pH curve intercept the pH axis (0.00 cm³ of NaOH(aq) added)?
Methylammonium chloride, CH₃NH₃Cl, is a salt. Which statement about this salt is correct?

options.text: It forms from HCl and CH₃NH₂, with water as a second product.
It forms from HCl and CH₃NH₂, with no water produced.
Its parent base is CH₃NH₃OH, since a base must contain OH.
Its parent base is CH₃NH₃⁺, the cation present in the salt.

questions.explanation: CH₃NH₂ + HCl → CH₃NH₃Cl. The amine accepts a proton on the lone pair of its nitrogen atom, so the only product is the salt. Its parent acid is HCl and its parent base is the amine CH₃NH₂.

questions.stem: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ HCl(aq) is titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH(aq) at 298 K until 50.0 cm³ of NaOH(aq) has been added. Which statement about the pH curve is correct?

options.text: After 25.0 cm³ the pH stays at 7, as all the acid is neutralized.
The pH rises by an equal amount for each 1.00 cm³ of NaOH(aq) added.
The curve starts near pH 13, the pH of the NaOH(aq) added.
At 25.0 cm³ the pH is 7, as only NaCl(aq) and water are present.

questions.explanation: 25.0 cm³ of NaOH(aq) contains the same amount as the HCl, so this is the equivalence point. The solution contains only NaCl and water, and a strong acid–strong base salt gives pH 7 at 298 K.

questions.stem: Solid magnesium oxide, MgO, is added to dilute nitric acid, HNO₃(aq). Which statement about what happens is correct?

options.text: MgO and HNO₃ react in a 1 : 1 mole ratio, as NaOH and HCl do too.
No reaction occurs, as MgO is not a base: it has no hydroxide ions.
Hydrogen gas is released, as acids give off H₂ in their reactions.
MgO and HNO₃ react in a 1 : 2 mole ratio, as O²⁻ accepts two H⁺.

questions.explanation: MgO(s) + 2HNO₃(aq) → Mg(NO₃)₂(aq) + H₂O(l). The oxide ion accepts two H⁺ (O²⁻ + 2H⁺ → H₂O), and the salt Mg(NO₃)₂ needs two NO₃⁻ for each Mg²⁺, so 1 mol of MgO reacts with 2 mol of HNO₃.

questions.stem: Solid sodium hydrogencarbonate, NaHCO₃, is added to dilute hydrochloric acid, HCl(aq). Which statement about the reaction is correct?

options.text: NaHCO₃ and HCl react in a 1 : 1 mole ratio, as HCO₃⁻ accepts one H⁺.
NaHCO₃ and HCl react in a 1 : 2 mole ratio, as carbonates do.
Only NaCl and water form, as neutralization gives salt and water.
Hydrogen gas is released, as acids give H₂ when they react.

questions.explanation: NaHCO₃(s) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g). HCO₃⁻ accepts one H⁺ and the product breaks down to water and carbon dioxide, which is released as a gas: HCO₃⁻ + H⁺ → H₂O + CO₂.

questions.stem: An aqueous solution at 298 K has [H⁺] = 5.0 × 10⁻⁶ mol dm⁻³. What is the pOH of the solution?
questions.explanation: pH = −log₁₀(5.0 × 10⁻⁶) = 5.30. At 298 K pH + pOH = 14.00, so pOH = 14.00 − 5.30 = 8.70. (Equivalently, [OH⁻] = Kw/[H⁺] = 2.0 × 10⁻⁹ mol dm⁻³ and pOH = −log₁₀(2.0 × 10⁻⁹) = 8.70.)

questions.stem: At 298 K the pKa of methanoic acid, HCOOH, is 3.75 and the pKa of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, is 4.76. Which statement about 0.10 mol dm⁻³ solutions of the two acids is correct?

options.text: Ethanoic acid is the stronger acid, as its pKa is the larger.
Both are ionized to the same extent, as both are weak acids.
Methanoic acid needs more NaOH(aq) to neutralize the same volume of it.
Methanoic acid is ionized to a greater extent than ethanoic acid.

questions.explanation: The smaller pKa means the larger Ka (1.8 × 10⁻⁴ against 1.7 × 10⁻⁵), so methanoic acid is the stronger acid and is ionized to a greater extent at the same concentration.

questions.stem: At 298 K the pKa of the ammonium ion, NH₄⁺, is 9.25 and the pKa of the methylammonium ion, CH₃NH₃⁺, is 10.66. Which statement about the bases NH₃ and CH₃NH₂ is correct?

options.text: CH₃NH₂ is the stronger base, and its pKb is 1.31.
CH₃NH₂ is the stronger base, since its pKb is 3.34.
NH₃ is the stronger base, since its pKb is 9.25.
NH₃ is the stronger base, as its pKb of 4.75 is larger.

questions.explanation: pKa + pKb = 14.00 for a conjugate pair at 298 K. pKb(CH₃NH₂) = 14.00 − 10.66 = 3.34 and pKb(NH₃) = 14.00 − 9.25 = 4.75. The smaller pKb means the stronger base, so CH₃NH₂ is stronger.

questions.stem: Aqueous solutions of sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃, and sodium hydrogencarbonate, NaHCO₃, each of concentration 0.10 mol dm⁻³, are prepared at 298 K. pKa(H₂CO₃) = 6.35 and pKa(HCO₃⁻) = 10.33. Which statement is correct?

options.text: NaHCO₃(aq) has the higher pH, since HCO₃⁻ has the larger pKa (10.33).
NaHCO₃(aq) is acidic, as HCO₃⁻ contains an H⁺ that it can donate.
Na₂CO₃(aq) has the higher pH, as CO₃²⁻ has the smaller pKb (3.67).
Both solutions are at pH 7, as each salt is a product of neutralization.

questions.explanation: CO₃²⁻ is the conjugate base of HCO₃⁻: pKb = 14.00 − 10.33 = 3.67. HCO₃⁻ as a base is the conjugate base of H₂CO₃: pKb = 14.00 − 6.35 = 7.65. CO₃²⁻ is the much stronger base, so CO₃²⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻ produces more OH⁻.

questions.stem: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ ethanoic acid (pKa = 4.76) is titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH(aq) at 298 K. What is the pH after 12.5 cm³ of NaOH(aq) has been added?
questions.explanation: 12.5 cm³ is half the equivalence volume (25.0 cm³). Half of the CH₃COOH has been converted to CH₃COO⁻, so [CH₃COOH] = [CH₃COO⁻], [H⁺] = Ka and pH = pKa = 4.76.

questions.stem:
An indicator, HInd, has pKa = 3.7:
HInd(aq) ⇌ H⁺(aq) + Ind⁻(aq)
HInd is red and Ind⁻ is yellow. What colour does the indicator show in a solution of pH 6.0, and why?

options.text: Yellow, as Ind⁻ predominates when the pH is above the pKa.
Red, as the solution is acidic, with its pH below 7.
Red, as HInd predominates when the pH is above the pKa.
Orange, as HInd and Ind⁻ are equal at equilibrium.

questions.explanation: At pH 6.0, [H⁺] = 1 × 10⁻⁶ mol dm⁻³, far below Ka = 2 × 10⁻⁴, so the equilibrium lies to the right: [Ind⁻]/[HInd] = Ka/[H⁺] ≈ 200. The solution shows the colour of Ind⁻, yellow.
